Start wide, narrow to the flows that matter. In Wireshark, work top-down:
Statistics > Protocol Hierarchy — what protocols exist and in what   proportion. Cleartext where you expected TLS, or a sliver of DNS carrying   most of the bytes, is the first tell.

Statistics > Endpoints — which hosts talk to the most peers; map internal   vs external at a glance.

A poorly designed survey produces precise measurements of the wrong thing - and because the numbers look rigorous, teams act on them with more confidence than they ever would on a hunch. This skill covers question construction, scale select
Order matters: constructs before questions, questions before flow, pilot before fielding - reversing any pair produces rework or, worse, fielded bias.
Leading - embeds an assumption. Fails: "How much did you enjoy the new feature?" Passes: "How would you rate your experience with the new feature?"
Loaded - carries emotional framing. Fails: "Do you agree that the cluttered interface slows you down?"

Order the flow. Screener first to qualify respondents; behavioral questions next (easier, less sensitive); attitudinal after; sensitive and demographic questions last - respondents who abandon mid-survey still yield usable data from earlier
